metadata.name: Iron-deficiency anaemia
metadata.emergency_level: Routine - but the CAUSE (e.g., GI cancer, severe bleeding) may be urgent
metadata.severity: Ranges from mild/asymptomatic to symptomatic; severity of the underlying cause matters most

overview.short_description: Anaemia due to insufficient iron for haemoglobin production, causing fatigue, breathlessness and pallor; a microcytic, hypochromic anaemia whose crucial task is finding the CAUSE (often blood loss).
overview.detailed_description: Iron-deficiency anaemia is very common. Symptoms are nonspecific; the diagnosis is confirmed by a low ferritin (with microcytosis). The essential clinical priority is to identify the cause - menstrual/pregnancy demands, dietary insufficiency, malabsorption (coeliac), or, importantly, gastrointestinal blood loss (including cancer). Treatment is iron replacement plus treating the cause.
overview.pathophysiology: Iron is required for haemoglobin synthesis; a negative iron balance (loss > intake/absorption) depletes stores (low ferritin), then reduces haemoglobin production, producing small (microcytic), pale (hypochromic) red cells.
overview.etiology: Blood loss (menstrual, gastrointestinal - ulcers, cancer, NSAIDs, hookworm in endemic areas), increased demand (pregnancy, infancy/growth), reduced intake (poor diet), and malabsorption (coeliac disease, post-gastric surgery, H. pylori).
overview.natural_history: Develops gradually as stores deplete; corrects with iron once the cause is addressed.
overview.prognosis: Excellent once treated and the cause managed; prognosis depends on the underlying cause (e.g., malignancy).

prevalence.value: One of the most common nutritional disorders worldwide; especially frequent in menstruating and pregnant women and young children.

incidence.value: High globally, particularly in low-resource settings.

mortality.value: Low directly; significant if the cause is serious (e.g., malignancy) or in severe anaemia.

epidemiology.age_groups: All ages; menstruating women, pregnancy, infants, and the elderly (GI causes).
epidemiology.sex_predominance: More common in women of reproductive age.
epidemiology.geographic_distribution: Worldwide; higher in areas with hookworm and dietary insufficiency.

risk_factors.alcohol: Excess associated with GI bleeding and poor diet.
risk_factors.genetic_factors: Coeliac disease predisposition; rare iron-refractory forms.
risk_factors.previous_diseases: Menorrhagia, peptic ulcer, coeliac disease, gastric surgery, chronic kidney disease, colorectal disease.

symptoms.symptom: Symptoms of the cause (menorrhagia, GI bleeding, weight loss)

negative_findings.finding: Normal ferritin (in the absence of inflammation)
negative_findings.why_important: A normal/high ferritin makes iron deficiency unlikely (but ferritin rises with inflammation)

negative_findings.finding: No GI symptoms, normal menstrual history, adequate diet
negative_findings.why_important: Guides where to look for the cause

history_questions.question: For women: heavy periods? For everyone: any GI symptoms, black stools, or blood in stool?
history_questions.why_ask: Blood loss is the commonest cause; GI loss may signal cancer

history_questions.question: Diet (vegetarian/vegan), and any coeliac symptoms (diarrhoea, bloating, weight loss)?
Any weight loss, change in bowel habit, or family history of GI cancer?
Are you pregnant?
history_questions.why_ask: Common cause with different management targets

physical_examination.expected_finding: Pallor; koilonychia, cheilitis, glossitis in chronic deficiency

physical_examination.examination: Abdominal examination and (as indicated) rectal examination
Cardiovascular (flow murmur, signs of heart failure if severe)
physical_examination.expected_finding: Tachycardia, flow murmur in significant anaemia

vital_signs.heart_rate: May be raised in significant anaemia
vital_signs.respiratory_rate: May be raised in severe anaemia

laboratory_tests.expected_result: Low Hb, low MCV/MCH (microcytic, hypochromic); anisocytosis/pencil cells on film
Low ferritin confirms iron deficiency; ferritin can be falsely normal/high with inflammation (check CRP; use transferrin saturation)

laboratory_tests.test_name: Coeliac serology (tissue transglutaminase); consider H. pylori

imaging.when_needed: Iron deficiency anaemia in men and postmenopausal women (and others without a clear cause) to exclude GI malignancy
imaging.expected_findings: Source of bleeding / malignancy if present

ecg.when_needed: If cardiac symptoms with severe anaemia

other_diagnostic_tests.endoscopy: Upper and lower GI endoscopy is the key investigation for the cause in unexplained iron deficiency
other_diagnostic_tests.biopsy: Duodenal biopsy for coeliac disease; biopsy of GI lesions
other_diagnostic_tests.culture: Stool tests / H. pylori as indicated

diagnostic_criteria.formal_criteria: Anaemia (low haemoglobin for age/sex) with laboratory evidence of iron deficiency, typically a LOW FERRITIN with microcytic, hypochromic indices. Where ferritin is confounded by inflammation, low transferrin saturation supports iron deficiency. Diagnosis is incomplete until the CAUSE is sought.

cutoff_values.value: Anaemia and ferritin thresholds are guideline/lab-specific; unexplained iron-deficiency anaemia in men and postmenopausal women warrants GI investigation (BSG).

differential_diagnosis.differences: Normal/high ferritin, chronic illness present, low transferrin saturation with normal/raised ferritin
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Is there a chronic inflammatory illness with normal ferritin?

differential_diagnosis.differences: Longstanding, disproportionately low MCV for mild anaemia, normal ferritin, family/ethnic background
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Is this longstanding with normal iron and relevant family history?

differential_diagnosis.differences: Weight loss, change in bowel habit, older age, rectal bleeding
differential_diagnosis.red_flags: Weight loss, altered bowel habit, rectal bleeding
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Any weight loss, bowel change, or rectal bleeding?

diagnostic_questions.question: Is there a clear blood-loss source (heavy periods) or GI symptoms/red flags?
diagnostic_questions.target_disease: Cause of iron deficiency (esp. GI malignancy)
diagnostic_questions.purpose: Find the cause - the most important step
diagnostic_questions.interpretation: GI red flags or unexplained IDA in men/postmenopausal women -> endoscopy

diagnostic_questions.question: Do the indices show low MCV and is ferritin low?

next_best_question.question: What is the likely source of blood loss, and are there GI red flags or coeliac features?
next_best_question.branching_logic: Menstrual/dietary -> iron + address source; men/postmenopausal or red flags -> urgent GI investigation; coeliac features -> coeliac serology

next_best_test.test: Ferritin (+ transferrin saturation/CRP) to confirm iron deficiency

red_flags.finding: Iron-deficiency anaemia in a man or postmenopausal woman without obvious cause
red_flags.immediate_action: Refer for urgent GI investigation (exclude cancer)

red_flags.finding: Weight loss, change in bowel habit, rectal bleeding, or abdominal/rectal mass
Severe symptomatic anaemia (chest pain, marked breathlessness, haemodynamic compromise)

red_flags.immediate_action: Urgent management of the bleeding source

referral_criteria.urgent_referral: Unexplained iron-deficiency anaemia (GI investigation); GI cancer red flags; severe symptomatic anaemia.
referral_criteria.routine_referral: Refractory anaemia, malabsorption work-up, or haematology input for uncertain diagnosis.

late: Complications of an untreated underlying cause (e.g., malignancy)

initial_management.supportive_care: Explain the diagnosis and the need to find the cause; dietary advice.
initial_management.medications: Canonical schema 1.3 guidance: use treatment_guidance.medication_options and its history-based safety checks. Candidate classes/options (not a prescription): Oral iron; Intravenous iron. No autonomous selection or dosing is allowed. Source IDs: BSG_IDA_2021.
initial_management.lifestyle_advice: Iron-rich diet (with vitamin C to aid absorption); take iron away from tea/calcium; address the underlying cause.
initial_management.follow_up: Recheck FBC to confirm response (e.g., Hb rise within weeks); ensure stores replenished; complete cause work-up.
initial_management.legacy_medications_pre_v13: Oral iron (e.g., ferrous sulfate/fumarate) - alternate-day dosing may improve tolerance/absorption; continue for ~3 months after Hb normalises to replenish stores. Intravenous iron if oral not tolerated/ineffective or malabsorption. Transfusion only for severe symptomatic anaemia. TREAT THE CAUSE (e.g., menorrhagia, coeliac disease, GI lesion).

patient_education.home_advice: Iron-deficiency anaemia means low iron, often from blood loss or diet. It causes tiredness, breathlessness and looking pale. Iron tablets treat it - take them as advised, continue for a few months after your blood count recovers, and expect darker stools. Just as important is finding the cause, which may need further tests. See a doctor promptly if you notice black stools, blood in your stool, or unexplained weight loss.
patient_education.home_advice_ar: فقر الدم بعوز الحديد يعني نقص الحديد، غالباً من فقدان الدم أو الغذاء، ويسبّب التعب وضيق النفس والشحوب. تعالجه حبوب الحديد - تناولها كما يُنصح، واستمرّ بضعة أشهر بعد تحسّن الدم، وتوقّع اسوداد البراز. ولا يقلّ أهميةً إيجاد السبب، وقد يحتاج فحوصات إضافية. راجع الطبيب سريعاً إذا لاحظت براز أسود، أو دماً في البراز، أو نقص وزن غير مبرّر.
patient_education.prevention: Iron-rich balanced diet; manage heavy periods; iron in pregnancy per guidance.
patient_education.warning_signs: Black/tarry stools, blood in stool, unexplained weight loss, severe breathlessness or chest pain.

prevention.lifestyle: Balanced iron-rich diet; treat/limit blood loss; iron supplementation in pregnancy/high-risk groups per guidance.
prevention.screening: Screening in pregnancy and selected high-risk groups.

evidence.evidence_level: High for iron replacement; strong for GI investigation of unexplained IDA.
evidence.guideline_strength: The main diagnosis/test and treatment direction was checked against the current guidance identified by BSG_IDA_2021; see evidence_review for scope and limitations. This does not verify every legacy narrative sentence.

treatment_guidance.treatment_goal: Correct iron deficiency and identify the cause, especially occult blood loss or malabsorption.
treatment_guidance.legacy_narrative_summary: Canonical schema 1.3 guidance: use treatment_guidance.medication_options and its history-based safety checks. Candidate classes/options (not a prescription): Oral iron; Intravenous iron. No autonomous selection or dosing is allowed. Source IDs: BSG_IDA_2021.
required_history_before_any_medication: age and weight where dosing is weight- or age-dependent
pregnancy or breastfeeding status when relevant
documented drug allergies and the exact reaction
all prescribed, OTC, herbal and recreational substances
major cardiovascular, respiratory, gastrointestinal and bleeding history
non_drug_measures: Treat the bleeding, dietary or malabsorption cause; do not label unexplained adult IDA as dietary without evaluation.

medication_options.when_to_consider: Confirmed iron deficiency when absorption and tolerance are adequate
medication_options.dose_policy: Dose is not inferred from this KB; use age, weight, renal/hepatic function, pregnancy status and the current local formulary/medicine label.

avoid_if: iron overload or anaemia not caused by iron deficiency
use_caution_if: active GI disease, severe constipation, malabsorption, ongoing bleeding, or interactions with levothyroxine/tetracyclines/quinolones/antacids
monitoring: haemoglobin response, ferritin/iron stores and tolerance; investigate failure to respond

medication_options.role: replacement when oral therapy is unsuitable
medication_options.when_to_consider: Intolerance, malabsorption, ongoing major loss or need for faster replacement under supervised care
medication_options.dose_policy: Dose is not inferred from this KB; use age, weight, renal/hepatic function, pregnancy status and the current local formulary/medicine label.

avoid_if: active serious hypersensitivity to the selected preparation
use_caution_if: active infection, pregnancy trimester, severe liver disease, prior infusion reaction, or phosphate-depletion risk
monitoring: observed infusion reaction, haemoglobin/iron response and phosphate for preparations/risk groups where indicated

medication_options.clinical_note: Requires product-specific hypersensitivity and phosphate monitoring policy.

medication_options.when_to_consider: Severe symptomatic/unstable anaemia under hospital protocols
medication_options.dose_policy: Dose is not inferred from this KB; use age, weight, renal/hepatic function, pregnancy status and the current local formulary/medicine label.
medication_options.clinical_note: Does not replace investigation or iron repletion.

procedures_referral_and_escalation: Urgent assessment for haemodynamic instability, active bleeding, chest pain/syncope or very severe symptoms; GI/gynaecological referral by age/sex/risk.
